paragraphs.text: Categorize plugins, MCP servers and skills into DeepSeek Harness agent presets.
# dsh-preset-categorizer

**Categorize plugins, MCP servers and skills into DeepSeek Harness agent
presets.**

DSH ships a fixed set of hand-written agent presets. This plugin reads what is
actually installed, g

roups the capabilities into categories, and registers
**one preset per category** with the host's ow

n preset registry — so a category
becomes a first-class entry in the GUI's preset picker.
It recognises **all three** kinds of capability, not just skills:
| Kind | What it sees | How it is scoped into a preset |

| **plugin** | loader entries backed by a package (`dsh-ffmpeg`, `dsh-image-gen`) | a plugin row |
|
**MCP** | loader entries backed by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` | an MCP row, with the server's ow

n config |
| **skill** | the skill directories under `~/.agents/skills*` | a skill-provider row for
kill** | the skill directories under `~/.agents/skills*` | a skill-provider row for a skill *root* |
## Why

A capability that lives in a profile's `bundles` is mounted into **every**
session, in every preset.

That is right for the harness's own machinery and
wrong for everything else: a plugin that adds six

tools costs every session
six tools' worth of schema, whether or not the session will ever use them

tools costs every session
six tools' worth of schema, whether or not the session will ever use them.

The built-in presets solve this by hand — `Creative` carries drawio, Blender
and FigCraft; `Office`

carries GenOffice; `Media` carries ffmpeg and Remotion.
That works until the set of installed capabi

lities changes, and then the
hand-written lists drift.
This plugin derives the same thing from the machine.

## How it behaves
Three rules, in the order they matter:

1. **It only adds.** Every preset it creates has an id starting with
`cat-`. If the host already has

a preset with that id, it is skipped and
reported. It never edits, replaces or removes an existing

preset, and it
never touches the profile's `package.json`.
2. **It never moves.** The plugin reports

what belongs where; it does not
unmount a capability from the host composition. Moving one is a dec

ision
with a cost — a plugin in `bundles` is also the one whose web UI loads — so
it stays with the

human.
3. **It adds no tools.** A categorizer that carried its own schemas would
spend the very budg
et it exists to protect.
### A missing package drops the row, not the preset

A preset that names a package the profile does not have mounts **broken** and
shows up red in the pi

cker. So the categorizer reads the profile's
`package.json` first and drops such rows:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Skills are scoped by root, not individually

A skill provider mounts a **directory**, and the skills on a machine usually
live in shared roots. S

o "genoffice but not mineru" is not expressible as a
preset — a category can only say "mount this ro

ot". Two categories claiming
the same root would mount the same provider twice, so the first wins an

d the
second is reported.
## Verify

**Registration is opt-in.** With the default config (`registerPresets` unset) the
plugin only writes

the report — `registered: false` — and adds no presets to the
picker. This machine runs in that mod

e deliberately (2026-10-31 report:
`registered: false`, 234 capabilities, 19 skills), so "registered

category
presets: 0" in `dsh-health` is not a fault. Set `registerPresets: true` in the
row config
to actually register the `cat-*` presets.

The plugin writes its own report, including the **host's own roster** with a
`broken` flag per prese

The category rules have unit tests:

## Configuration

The categories live in `lib/categories.js` as plain data. Each one declares
what it matches and what
its preset carries:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

* `include` / `exclude` — glob patterns (`*`, `?`) matched against the
capability's id, name and pac

kage. `exclude` wins.
* `mcpRows` — literal loader rows. An MCP server is mounted by *config*
(serve

rName, transport, command/url), which cannot be derived from a package
name.
* `skillRoot` — an abso
lute path to a skill directory to mount.
The first matching category wins, so the order of the list is meaningful.
## Safety

* **No network.** The plugin makes no outbound request of any kind.
* **No subprocess.** No `exec`,

no `spawn`, no `eval`.
* **Reads only**: the skill directories under `~/.agents/skills*` and the
pro

file's `package.json`.
* **Writes one file**: `~/.dsh/preset-categorizer-report.json`, containing
na

mes and counts only — no absolute paths, no credentials.
* **Touches nothing else.** No profile mani

fest, no patch file, no existing
preset.
